name: pagination
purpose: Page navigation for paged data: a labelled <nav> of native buttons (previous/next, optional first/last, page numbers with ellipses), an optional localized result summary, an optional rows-per-page <select>, polite announcements after page changes, and a compact 'Page 3 of 10' layout in narrow containers.
whenToUse: Tables and result lists split into pages, where users need to know and choose their position.
Server-paged data where the total or page count is known.
whenNotToUse: Feeds consumed sequentially: use 'Load more' or infinite scrolling with a clear end.
Fewer items than one page: render the list without pagination.
responsive: The host is a size container. Below 30rem of inline space the page numbers are hidden and 'Page 3 of 10' is shown between previous and next. Buttons keep the minimum touch-target size; summary, controls, and the size select wrap.
rtl: Logical layout follows the document direction. Direction icons (chevrons) are mirrored when direction is rtl (configured) or the element is in an rtl context (:dir(rtl)).
theme: The current page uses color-selected / color-selected-text with a color-primary border and semibold weight (not color alone). Hover uses color-hover; focus uses the shared focus ring. Forced-colors mode renders the current page with Highlight / HighlightText.
security: All text is rendered with textContent. No HTML parsing. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. The component never fetches data; consumers load pages on aui-change.

budgets.budget: < 1 ms in headless Chromium (rendered items are bounded by siblingCount and boundaryCount)

performance.testedScale: getPageItems exhaustively tested for page counts 0 to 30 across 7 sibling/boundary combinations; 12,345 items in the unit tests.

limitations: No direct page-number input ('go to page').
The compact layout breakpoint (30rem container width) is fixed in the stylesheet.
Changing the page size keeps the first item of the current page visible; consumers wanting page 1 can call setPage(1).
unsupported: Cursor-based pagination without a known page count (use previous/next buttons directly).
Links (href) for page items; pages are buttons that emit aui-change.
antiPatterns: Hiding previous/next at the bounds instead of disabling them (the layout jumps).
Pagination for a handful of items.
Resetting to page 1 on every data refresh.
